meta.name: GitHub Advanced Security Certification
meta.notes: Initial pack: 12 questions covering GHAS product surface — code scanning (CodeQL default and advanced setup, SARIF), secret scanning (alerts, push protection, custom patterns), Dependabot (alerts vs security updates vs version updates, dependency review), Copilot Autofix, alert triage permissions, CodeQL query packs, and GHAS enablement on Enterprise Cloud. Answer positions balanced 3/3/3/3 across A/B/C/D. Every explanation refutes every distractor.

questions.question: Which set of features is included when a repository has GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) enabled on GitHub Enterprise Cloud?
options: Code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review
SAML SSO, IP allow lists, and the audit log streaming API
Codespaces prebuilds, GitHub Pages, and Discussions
Included Actions minutes, Git LFS storage, and Copilot Business seats
questions.explanation: GHAS is the security-features add-on: it turns on CodeQL-based code scanning, secret scanning (with push protection and custom patterns), and PR-time dependency review. SAML SSO, IP allow lists, and audit-log streaming are Enterprise Cloud administrative features that ship independent of GHAS. Codespaces, Pages, and Discussions are platform features unrelated to the security add-on. Actions minutes, LFS storage, and Copilot Business are separately billed products and are not part of GHAS.

questions.question: A team wants to enable CodeQL code scanning on dozens of repositories using GitHub's curated query suites, without editing a workflow file in each repo. Which option best fits?
options: Advanced setup, committing a `codeql-analysis.yml` workflow per repo
Default setup for code scanning, enabled per repo or across the org
Nightly `codeql database analyze` runs from a self-hosted runner script
A branch protection rule that requires a CodeQL status check
questions.explanation: Default setup enables code scanning with a single click — GitHub auto-detects languages, selects a curated query suite, and manages the workflow without a committed YAML file; org owners can also roll it out across all repos with GHAS. Advanced setup exists but requires committing and maintaining a workflow file per repo, which is exactly what the team wants to avoid. Running the CodeQL CLI from a cron script bypasses managed workflows and does not use default query suites. A branch protection rule can enforce a check but does not enable or configure CodeQL — the scan must already exist for the check to appear.

questions.question: A developer's `git push` is rejected at the remote with a message that a secret was detected and the push blocked. Which GHAS capability produced this behavior?
options: A required pull request review defined in branch protection
Dependabot security updates opening a follow-up PR
Secret scanning push protection
Copilot Autofix rewriting the offending commit
questions.explanation: Push protection is the secret-scanning feature that intercepts a push at the remote when a high-confidence supported pattern is detected and refuses the push unless the developer explicitly bypasses it with a documented reason. Branch protection can require reviews but does not inspect content for secrets and cannot reject a push based on regex matches. Dependabot security updates open PRs after an alert on a vulnerable dependency; they never inspect push contents or block a push. Copilot Autofix suggests remediations for code-scanning alerts and does not rewrite commits or block pushes.

questions.question: The dependency graph shows that a project depends on a package with a known CVE. Which Dependabot capability automatically opens a pull request to upgrade that dependency to a patched version?
options: The dependency graph itself, which raises PRs when a manifest is edited
Dependabot alerts, which post a PR alongside the alert body
Dependabot version updates, using `dependabot.yml` schedules
Dependabot security updates, once alerts are enabled on the repo
questions.explanation: Dependabot security updates are the mechanism that reacts to a Dependabot alert by opening a targeted PR that bumps the vulnerable dependency to a patched version; enabling alerts is the prerequisite. The dependency graph is a read-only inventory of manifests and lockfiles — it detects dependencies but never opens PRs. Dependabot alerts are notifications describing the vulnerability; they do not by themselves author remediation PRs. Dependabot version updates open PRs on a fixed schedule to keep dependencies current whether or not there is a vulnerability, so they are not the vulnerability-driven mechanism the question describes.

questions.question: During a pull request, where can a reviewer see code scanning alerts introduced by that PR without leaving the PR view?
options: Inline annotations in the Files changed tab and a summary in Checks
Only in the repository's Security tab under Code scanning alerts
Only via a webhook to an external issue tracker
As commit-status entries that link out to a separate scan dashboard
questions.explanation: Code scanning surfaces new alerts introduced by a PR as inline annotations on the diff in Files changed and rolls them up in the PR's Checks summary, letting reviewers triage without navigating away. The Security tab does list alerts, but it is not the only surface — that answer is wrong because reviewers can also see them on the PR. A webhook can be added for external systems, but PR-time visibility does not require one and it is not GitHub's default surface. A commit status can link out, but code scanning uses Checks with rich inline annotations rather than a status that only points to an external dashboard.

questions.question: A team runs a third-party SAST scanner in CI and wants the findings to appear in GitHub's Code scanning alerts UI. What must the workflow upload to GitHub?
options: A JUnit XML test report attached as a workflow artifact
A SARIF results file, typically via the `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` action
A CodeQL database bundle produced by `codeql database create`
A dependency manifest file consumed by the dependency graph
questions.explanation: Code scanning ingests results in SARIF 2.1.0 format; uploading a SARIF file via the `upload-sarif` action or the Code Scanning API is how any tool — CodeQL or third-party — surfaces alerts in the Code scanning UI. JUnit XML is a test-report format that GitHub does not interpret as security findings. A CodeQL database is the raw dataset used to run CodeQL queries; it is not what you upload to publish alerts, and it is CodeQL-specific rather than a third-party integration format. A dependency manifest feeds the dependency graph and Dependabot, not code scanning.

questions.question: Your organization uses an internal API token whose format is a company-specific prefix followed by 40 hex characters. How do you make GitHub detect that pattern in commits and existing repo history?
options: Add the token format to a repository `.gitignore` file
Register token maintainers as reviewers via CODEOWNERS
Define a custom secret scanning pattern at the org or repo level
List the pattern in a `dependabot.yml` file under `secret-patterns`
questions.explanation: Custom secret scanning patterns let an org, enterprise, or repo owner add regexes for proprietary secret formats; when saved, GitHub runs a dry run first and then scans both new pushes and existing history, and the pattern can also participate in push protection once promoted. A `.gitignore` file changes which files Git tracks but does no content inspection and applies only to untracked files. CODEOWNERS routes review requests to specific users but does not detect or block secrets. `dependabot.yml` configures Dependabot updates for dependencies and has no `secret-patterns` key.

questions.question: A security engineer maintains house-specific CodeQL queries that many repositories should consume. What is the recommended way to distribute and version those queries?
options: Copy the `.ql` files into every consuming repository
Attach them to release assets and download at scan time
Publish them as an npm package that the workflow installs
Publish them as a CodeQL query pack and reference it from workflows
questions.explanation: CodeQL query packs are the first-class distribution unit for CodeQL queries: they carry a `qlpack.yml`, are versioned with semver, and can be published to the GitHub Container Registry and referenced from a code-scanning workflow's `packs:` input — one authoritative copy consumed by many repos. Copying `.ql` files into every repo defeats versioning and drifts quickly. Release assets can host arbitrary files but bypass the query-pack tooling that resolves dependencies and versions correctly. npm is not the CodeQL distribution mechanism; the CodeQL CLI and Actions do not resolve queries from npm.

questions.question: A developer wants to dismiss a code scanning alert as `Won't fix` from the alert page. What repository permission do they need?
options: Write access to the repository is sufficient to dismiss alerts
Only repository administrators can dismiss alerts
Only the alert's original committer can dismiss it
Organization owner permissions are required for any dismissal
questions.explanation: Dismissing a code scanning alert (with `False positive`, `Used in tests`, or `Won't fix`) requires write access to the repository — the same permission that lets a user manage most repo content, so it does not need admin. Restricting dismissal to administrators only would block normal triage by the development team and is not how the permission is scoped. There is no requirement that the original committer dismiss the alert; anyone with the right role can. Organization owner is a much broader permission than needed and is not a prerequisite here.

questions.question: How does the Dependency review feature help reviewers evaluate a pull request that changes a project's dependencies?
options: It automatically merges dependency-only PRs when tests pass
It shows dependency additions, removals, version bumps, and any vulnerabilities or license issues introduced by the diff
It replaces the repository's dependency graph while the PR is open
It generates a full SPDX SBOM and posts it as a PR comment on every push
questions.explanation: Dependency review renders a per-PR summary of manifest and lockfile changes and flags any newly introduced vulnerabilities or license issues, giving reviewers explicit context before merge; a Dependency review action can also fail the check on configured severity or license policy. It does not auto-merge PRs — merge policy is controlled by branch protection and Auto-merge, not by dependency review. It does not replace the dependency graph; the graph continues to inventory the repo's dependencies while the PR is open. It does not automatically generate an SBOM comment; SBOM export is a separate, on-demand action.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Copilot Autofix for code scanning alerts?
options: It auto-merges pull requests whose Copilot fix passes tests
It replaces manual code review of the affected files by security staff
It proposes a suggested fix for many CodeQL alerts that a reviewer can commit from the PR
It retrains the CodeQL model on the repository's own bug history
questions.explanation: Copilot Autofix generates suggested code changes for many supported CodeQL alerts, and a reviewer can accept the suggestion directly from the PR or the alert view — human decision stays in the loop. It does not auto-merge PRs; merge behavior is governed by branch protection and Auto-merge settings, not by Autofix. It does not replace security review — a person still evaluates and commits (or edits) the fix. It does not retrain CodeQL on the repository's history; CodeQL analysis is powered by curated query packs, not repo-tailored model training.

questions.question: An Enterprise Cloud organization has purchased GHAS licenses. A repository administrator wants to turn GHAS features on for one specific repository. Where should they enable it?
options: Add the `github-advanced-security` action to the default branch workflow
Create a `SECURITY.md` file at the repository root
Invite the enterprise security team as repository collaborators
Toggle `GitHub Advanced Security` on in the repository's `Settings → Code security and analysis`
questions.explanation: GHAS is enabled per repository from `Settings → Code security and analysis` (or org-wide from the org-level equivalent), where the admin toggles the feature on and consumes one licensed committer seat — that action then unlocks code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review UI in the repo. There is no `github-advanced-security` action; features are not enabled by referencing a workflow step. `SECURITY.md` publishes a security policy for reporting vulnerabilities and does not enable any scanning feature. Adding collaborators grants access but does not turn on the paid GHAS features on the repository.
